hints: Focus on what a catalytic converter is trying to fix, the harmful CO, unburnt hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides in exhaust.
Notice that reaction 1 oxidises a hydrocarbon to CO2 and water, and reaction 2 turns NO and CO into harmless N2 and CO2.
Ask yourself if sulfur oxides are cleaned up this way, and check which combination keeps only the CO, hydrocarbon and NOx clean-up reactions.
walkthrough:
**Recall the job of the converter**

Think of it as a clean-up unit. It oxidises toxic CO and unburnt fuel, and it reduces nitrogen oxides to harmless nitrogen.

Typical changes: $\text{CO} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2$, $\text{hydrocarbon} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{NO}_x \rightarrow \text{N}_2$

**Check reaction 1**

This is complete combustion of octane, a model for petrol.

$$\text{C}_8\text{H}_{18} + 12\tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 8\text{CO}_2 + 9\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This is exactly what happens to unburnt hydrocarbons on the platinum and palladium catalyst, so 1 is correct.

**Check reaction 2**

This uses CO to reduce NO.

$$2\text{NO} + 2\text{CO} \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + 2\text{CO}_2$$
Both pollutants disappear and give harmless $\text{N}_2$ plus $\text{CO}_2$. This redox reaction on rhodium is the key de-NOx reaction, so 2 is correct.

**Check reaction 3**

$$\text{NO} + \text{SO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NO}_2 + \text{SO}_2$$
This just swaps one pollutant pair for another and does not remove CO, hydrocarbons or NOx. Sulfur is removed from fuel before use, not by this reaction, so 3 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusion**

Only 1 and 2 occur. That combination matches the correct option.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three reactions. Reactions 1 and 2 are correct clean-up reactions, but reaction 3 involving $\text{SO}_3$ to $\text{SO}_2$ is not a catalytic converter reaction.
options.B: Correct because only 1 and 2 occur. Reaction 1 oxidises unburnt hydrocarbon to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and reaction 2 reduces $\text{NO}$ with $\text{CO}$ to $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$, the two main jobs of the converter.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes reaction 3 and misses reaction 1. Reaction 3 is not involved, while oxidation of unburnt hydrocarbons in reaction 1 is a major converter reaction.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only reaction 1. While hydrocarbon oxidation is correct, it leaves out the equally important reduction of $\text{NO}$ to $\text{N}_2$ in reaction 2.
